risks.risk: Dependence on raw jute crop availability and price volatility
risks.note: An insufficient raw jute crop during the year created a difficult situation for the jute industry throughout the season; prices started rising from the beginning of the season and the industry witnessed unprecedented levels of raw jute prices, well above the statutory minimum rates, directly affecting the Company's cost base.

risks.risk: Regulatory rationing of the raw material market
risks.note: The Jute Commissioner imposed raw jute stock limits on the jute industry throughout the season to ensure equitable distribution within the industry and to prevent hoarding by mills and traders, indicating the Company's key input is subject to government-directed allocation during periods of scarcity.

The Company does not have any subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as on 31st March 2026, and none became or ceased to be one during the year, meaning all business risk sits within the single standalone entity.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Current-year performance will depend largely on availability of the raw jute crop; management expects a much better crop compared to the previous season.
- The year is likely to remain challenging, particularly during July and August, when uncertainty regarding raw jute availability may persist.
- Other income remains uncertain as it may be influenced by the outcome of the West Asia conflict, but management believes the overall outlook for the current year would be stable.
- Elevated oil prices from the West Asia conflict are expected to raise the cost of plastic packaging materials, which may improve the competitive position of jute-based packaging products.
- Sustainability and environmental concerns are expected to continue driving preference towards eco-friendly and biodegradable jute packaging, supporting long-term industry prospects.
- High raw jute prices during the last jute season are likely to encourage farmers to increase jute acreage in the current season, improving raw jute availability.
- Domestic and export markets may shift towards alternative packaging materials due to high jute product prices and supply uncertainties.
- Improvement in domestic demand during the year, in terms of both quantity and realisation, contributed to revenue growth, while overseas sales were affected by higher finished-product prices from steep raw jute price and freight increases and tariff-related issues.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- The Company continues to focus on employee development through regular in-house training programmes aimed at enhancing working knowledge, technical competence and overall skill sets of employees, alongside employee welfare schemes.
- The Board recommended a final dividend for FY26 at ₹25 per ordinary share (250%), subject to member approval at the AGM, up sharply from the prior year's payout; the directors did not propose to transfer any amount to reserves out of FY26 profits. Members are also being asked to approve a resolution permitting payment of commission to non-executive directors (including independent directors), capped at 1% of net profits, at the Board's discretion in each financial year.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26 the Company incurred capital expenditure towards installation of a rooftop Solar Power Plant with a capacity of 2,274.48 kWp, which contributes approximately 12-15 percent of the power requirement. Machineries required for strengthening manufacturing efficiency were also purchased. The Company operated well below its installed capacity during the year due to economic conditions and the raw jute supply scenario, with no new plant/line expansion disclosed.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on raw jute crop availability and price volatility — An insufficient raw jute crop during the year created a difficult situation for the jute industry throughout the season; prices started rising from the beginning of the season and the industry witnessed unprecedented levels of raw jute prices, well above the statutory minimum rates, directly affecting the Company's cost base.
- Regulatory rationing of the raw material market — The Jute Commissioner imposed raw jute stock limits on the jute industry throughout the season to ensure equitable distribution within the industry and to prevent hoarding by mills and traders, indicating the Company's key input is subject to government-directed allocation during periods of scarcity.
- No subsidiary/associate diversification — The Company does not have any subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as on 31st March 2026, and none became or ceased to be one during the year, meaning all business risk sits within the single standalone entity.
